Fixed. The bug was in the default (slice-based) `Labels.DropMetricName` in model/labels/labels.go:425 — `append(ls[:nameIdx], ls[nameIdx+1:]...)` shifted elements in the backing array in place, corrupting any other `Labels` sharing that array (which happens in range queries when `mat[i].Metric = mat[i].Metric.DropMetricName()` is applied to series built from a shared backing array, producing the duplicate `{__address__="bar", job="1", job="1"}` series).

The fix (model/labels/labels.go:346) now:
- keeps the `ls[1:]` fast path when `__name__` is the first label (no allocation, no mutation of preceding elements),
- allocates a new slice when `__name__` is in the middle, leaving the original labels untouched,
- drops the now-unnecessary validation bookkeeping that was only feeding dead branches.

Validated: `go test -count=1 ./model/labels/ ./promql/` all pass in the container, and a direct reproduction of the issue scenario shows the original labels are no longer mutated by `DropMetricName`. (Note: `go.mod` was accidentally overwritten by a verification command and has been restored via git; only `model/labels/labels.go` remains modified.)
